_meta.source_document: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Rural District, Karnataka State (titled 'cpcpDISTRICT ENVIRONMENTAL PLAN FOR BENGALURRURAL DISTRICT')
_meta.published: April 2022 (s3waas upload path 2022/04); office of the Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Rural District.
_meta.data_as_on: Industrial / KSPCB F-Register data explicitly 'as on 31-03-2021' (p.58). District profile uses 2011 Census base population. Action-plan completion timelines run 31-03-2022 to 31-03-2023. Cited throughout below as 'DEP 2021' (the 31-03-2021 F-Register cut-off year), consistent with the 2022 publication.
_meta.extraction_method: PDF is a CamScanner/iLovePDF SCANNED IMAGE (no text layer; pdftotext returned empty). Rendered to PNG at 200-350 dpi with pdftoppm and OCR'd with tesseract; the three load-bearing pages (solid-waste p.7, domestic-sewage/STP p.55, underground-sewerage p.57, industrial p.58) were ALSO read visually from the rendered page images to confirm every numeric cell, because tesseract garbled the rotated/boxed tables. Figures below are taken from the visual reads, not the raw OCR.
_meta.structure_note: This DEP is organised PER ULB (Urban Local Body), not per valley/basin. The five ULBs are Hoskote CMC, Doddaballapura CMC, Nelamangala CMC, Devanahalli Town MC and Vijayapura Town MC. Of the three Arkavathi/Kumudavathi-headwater taluks requested, Doddaballapura (Arkavathi headwaters near Nandi/Doddaballapur hills), Nelamangala (Kumudavathi headwaters) and Devanahalli are extracted below. Hoskote and Vijayapura are in the Dakshina Pinakini (Pennar) / north catchment respectively and are not part of the Arkavathi-basin scope, so they are recorded only as supporting context inside source 'says' strings.
_meta.industrial_caveat: Industrial effluent, ETP/CETP and industry-count figures in this DEP are reported DISTRICT-WIDE ONLY (all of Bengaluru Rural), not split per taluk/ULB. The same district-wide industrial block is therefore attached to each Arkavathi taluk with an explicit 'district-wide, not taluk-level' label on each metric. Do not present these as per-taluk values.
_meta.solid_waste_caveat: The DEP's solid-waste section gives per-ULB GENERATION (tons/day) cleanly (p.7) but does NOT publish a per-ULB 'quantity processed' or 'legacy/dumpsite tonnage' figure. The downstream tables are gap-analysis percentages (door-to-door collection %, segregation, composting, bulk-waste). 'Processed' and 'legacy waste' are therefore flagged as not-tabulated rather than invented.

doddaballapura.name: Doddaballapura (City Municipal Council / taluk)
doddaballapura.coverage: Bengaluru Rural DEP 2021 (data as on 31-03-2021; pub. 2022)
doddaballapura.headline: Doddaballapura CMC generates ~5.0 MLD of sewage against a 12 MLD STP, but an incomplete UGD network (20% still uncovered) means sewage bypasses the plant; it is the district's largest solid-waste generator at 35 TPD

streams.summary: 5.0 MLD wastewater vs a 12 MLD existing STP; present sewage flow ~5 MLD. On paper capacity is adequate, but the DEP's gap analysis says the UGD network is incomplete so missing links bypass the STP and must be intercepted and diverted. 80% of the UGD network is provided; 20% still to be completed.

metrics.label: STP capacity vs generation
metrics.value: Adequate on paper; no MLD shortfall stated (DEP 2021)

metrics.label: Compliance / treatment gap
metrics.value: Incomplete UGD -> sewage bypasses STP via missing links (DEP 2021)

sources.source: Bengaluru Rural DEP 2021 - Domestic sewage gap & action plan table (p.55)
sources.says: City Municipal Council, Doddaballapura: Quantity of waste water present 5.0 MLD; Existing STP Capacity 12 MLD; Present Sewage Flow rate 5 MLD. Gap Analysis: 'Due to incomplete UGD network connected to STP there is a missing links bypassing the STP. Thus, these missing links must be intercepted and diverted to existing STP for treatment and Disposal. The existing STP is adequate.'
sources.citation: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Rural District, Domestic Sewage gap analysis table, p.55

sources.citation: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Rural District, Underground sewerage network table, p.57

streams.summary: The DEP reports industrial effluent ONLY at the district level (all of Bengaluru Rural), not per taluk. District-wide: 151 industries discharge wastewater generating 14.354 MLD; NIL treated industrial wastewater is discharged to nalas/rivers; 2 Common Effluent Treatment Facilities exist; 134 industries meet discharge standards and 26 do not.

Common Effluent Treatment Facilities: 2 Nos. No of Industries meeting discharge Standards: 134 Nos. No of Industries not meeting discharge Standards: 26 Nos.
